fit: Parkinson minor phenomenon interviews and resting fMRI
assessment: The journal article uses 18 Parkinson participants with minor visual phenomena, 14 without hallucinations and 31 controls. Clinician assessments distinguish presence and passage phenomena, illusions or pareidolias, with overlap across categories. The paper describes cross-sectional functional connectivity and concurrent cognitive scores. The 2025 preprint describes the same Parkinson cohort.

fit: initial clinical phenotype and time to dementia in a Peruvian cohort
assessment: The retrospective cohort stratifies dementia with Lewy bodies by initial cognitive, motor or behavioral symptoms. Cognitive-onset patients progressed to dementia sooner in the observed cohort. Onset phenotype and later clinical domain observations provide no food-timed changes in visual episode count.

fit: expert and trial context on subcutaneous levodopa adverse effects
assessment: This expert and trial synthesis covers initiation and maintenance of a subcutaneous medication and discusses prior hallucinations or psychosis as clinical context. The reviewed exposures concern drug administration, without a fig intervention or an original food-timed episode estimate.

fit: Parkinson psychosis review and clinically distinct triggers
assessment: The European perspective summarizes hallucinations, delusions and management of potential clinical and medication triggers. Its underlying evidence involves disease progression and drug or concurrent illness contexts. It offers no measured dried fig or dietary timing comparison.

fit: hydrocephalus meeting member with a visual presentation
assessment: The full published proceedings contain independent hydrocephalus reports. One diagnostic member notes visual hallucinations and falls in a case with imaging-supported possible normal-pressure hydrocephalus. A separate shunt member tracks neuropsychiatric and functional measures. Neither measures a dried fig exposure, and the clinical cases are distinct.

fit: two Parkinson colitis cases and changes in medication route
assessment: Two case reports and a literature review track microscopic colitis during oral dopaminergic therapy and resolution following treatment changes. The observations concern bowel symptoms and drug routes. Dietary fig and visual episode frequency are outside the comparison.

fit: timed diagnostic chart features with linked neuropathology
assessment: The autopsy-linked study uses onset data for clinical features from 949 patients who developed parkinsonism within three years of disease onset. The model predicts later neuropathological classification using clinical history. Occurrence or onset of symptoms provides no culinary exposure or episode-rate comparison.

fit: patient-specific metabolic predictions and dietary inference limits
assessment: The study applies genome-scale models to infer patient-specific metabolite secretion patterns and summarize candidate Parkinson biomarkers. Predicted metabolites, including vitamin-related compounds, are distinct from a measured dietary source. It records no dried fig intake or visual episode frequency after food.

fit: tissue findings and clinical hallucinations reported in prior studies
assessment: The review compares proximity ligation approaches to characterize alpha-synuclein oligomers. It cites a tissue association with visual hallucination presence in dementia with Lewy bodies. This is a cited neuropathological association without a culinary exposure or clinical recurrence measure.

fit: clinical sleep and psychiatric onset in dementia with Lewy bodies
assessment: The 359-person clinical series groups dementia with Lewy bodies participants by sleep profiles and relates them to disease onset characteristics. A psychiatric-onset group and sleep symptom prevalence do not supply a dried fig exposure or a rate of recurrent visual episodes.

fit: congress members on separate diet and Parkinson psychosis questions
assessment: The complete published congress supplement contains separate whole-diet protocols, a nutrition education pilot, dietary risk associations and medication or surgery psychosis analyses. No inspected member exposed a Parkinson cohort to dried figs and tracked visual episode frequency. The whole-diet, constipation and psychosis findings belong to distinct sets of participants.

fit: nonmotor features across PSP and Parkinson diagnostic groups
assessment: The cross-sectional comparison tracks synuclein-related and nonmotor features in Parkinson disease and two progressive supranuclear palsy phenotypes. The comparison of symptom patterns and biomarker status does not measure timing after dried fig or Parkinson visual event rates.

fit: structural MRI comparison with matching medRxiv cohort
assessment: The journal results analyze 83 people with dementia with Lewy bodies and 86 controls after quality control, as in the May preprint. Cortical shape and thickness, regional transcriptomic maps and connectivity are measured or compared. The design contains no food exposure or within-person visual episode-rate outcome.

fit: visual hallucinations and real-world infusion discontinuation
assessment: Of 50 consecutive advanced Parkinson patients who initiated subcutaneous treatment, two discontinued after visual hallucinations and both had prior psychosis. This implementation report counts discontinuations, without a controlled dietary exposure or recurrent visual episode frequencies.

fit: practice observations separate medication, meals and adverse reports
assessment: The article draws on German clinicians' practical experience with subcutaneous levodopa and discusses protein and motor OFF timing as a possible clinical consideration. The clinical guidance and adverse-event discussion are separate. No individual dried fruit or food-timed visual outcome is tracked.

fit: distinguishing delusions from clinical visual hallucinations
assessment: The review includes seven eligible studies. It treats delusions, delusional misidentification and visual hallucinations as related but distinct outcomes. The source includes no dried fig intervention and supplies no fig-attributed recurrent visual episode counts.

fit: fasting blood biomarkers by minor Parkinson hallucination status
assessment: The cross-sectional study compares 34 Parkinson participants with minor hallucinations with 65 without them. Mean fasting plasma homocysteine was higher in the minor-hallucination group. Folate, B12, drug dose and disease duration are separate measures. The study does not measure dried fig intake or rates of episodes after a specific food.
